storm_spirits.museum: De Morgan Collection / De Morgan Foundation
storm_spirits.story: The first red-winged figure seizes attention, then the painting reveals Rain and Thunderclouds. A hidden calm centre opposes the violence of the sea. End on the entire authentic painting in contemplative stillness. Interpretation follows the De Morgan Foundation and is not presented as proven artist intent.

scenes.intent: Start with the authentic red-winged spirit of Lightning, a vivid human presence against the dark storm
The painted golden lightning bolts emerge from the figure's hand
The red feathers turn from ornament into the central force of the composition
First entire composition reveals the three allegorical forces without distortion
Thunderclouds in blue dress and dark wings seem to merge with the storm sky
A quiet hand and blue cloth provide a human counterpoint to the violence
Rain pours from the left, contrasting warm gold fabric and grey water
The inexhaustible stream of rain connects the spirit to the foaming sea
Rocks and breakers dominate the lower painting as the musical tension rises
White water cuts through the dark rock masses with a diagonal movement painted into the work
Small calm clearing at the centre carries the counter-idea of refuge
Return to Lightning with new context: energy now contrasts with a possible sanctuary
The dark storm cloud forms an expressive ceiling over the allegorical figures
The rainy coast and two forces share the scene in one readable spatial connection
The red wings and blue drapery are briefly reunited before the final release
Whole genuine painting held still to complete the contrast between chaos and refuge
